questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If she had negotiated her salary, she wouldn't be struggling financially now.
If she negotiated her salary, she wouldn't be struggling financially now.
If she had negotiated her salary, she wouldn't have struggled financially now.
If she had negotiated her salary, she won't struggle financially now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect (past condition), would + base verb (present result): 'If she had negotiated..., she wouldn't be struggling now.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Employee turnover will keep rising unless managers won't improve working conditions.
Employee turnover will keep rising unless managers improve working conditions.
Employee turnover will keep rising unless that managers improve working conditions.
Employee turnover will keep rising without managers improve working conditions.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if...not' and is followed by an affirmative clause: 'unless managers improve working conditions.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Several new policies has been introduced this year.
Several new policies have introduced this year.
Several new policies have been introduced this year.
Several new policies have being introduced this year.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle: 'have been introduced this year.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This staffing shortage should resolved immediately.
This staffing shortage should being resolved immediately.
This staffing shortage should be resolve immediately.
This staffing shortage should be resolved immediately.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: 'should be resolved immediately.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "Please submit the report by Friday.")
options: The manager told us to submit the report by Friday.
The manager told us submit the report by Friday.
The manager said us to submit the report by Friday.
The manager told us that submit the report by Friday.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell + object + to + base verb: 'told us to submit the report by Friday.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "You should update your resume regularly.")
options: She suggested to update my resume regularly.
She suggested updating my resume regularly.
She suggested me updating my resume regularly.
She suggested that I updating my resume regularly.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund or 'that + subject + base verb': 'suggested updating my resume regularly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company which she works for it values employee wellbeing.
The company for that she works values employee wellbeing.
The company for which she works values employee wellbeing.
The company she works for which values employee wellbeing.
questions.explanation: In formal style, the preposition moves before 'which': 'the company for which she works.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The report publishing last week revealed low employee satisfaction.
The report published last week reveal low employee satisfaction.
The report which published last week revealed low employee satisfaction.
The report published last week revealed low employee satisfaction.
questions.explanation: A passive meaning reduces 'which was published' to the past participle alone: 'The report published last week...'

questions.topic: Modal verbs of past deduction (must have)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The team must have missed the project deadline.
The team must missed the project deadline.
The team must have miss the project deadline.
The team must has missed the project deadline.
questions.explanation: Past deduction: must have + past participle: 'must have missed the deadline.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company should acted sooner to prevent the layoffs.
The company should have acted sooner to prevent the layoffs.
The company should have act sooner to prevent the layoffs.
The company should has acted sooner to prevent the layoffs.
questions.explanation: Past regret/criticism: should have + past participle: 'should have acted sooner.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Remote work rose significantly over the past few years.
Remote work has risen significantly over the past few years.
Remote work have risen significantly over the past few years.
Remote work have rose significantly over the past few years.
questions.explanation: 'Over the past few years' links the past to the present, so present perfect is used: 'has risen significantly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: By the time the meeting started, most employees left the office.
By the time the meeting had started, most employees left the office.
By the time the meeting started, most employees have already left the office.
By the time the meeting started, most employees had already left the office.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: 'most employees had already left the office.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The board is meeting next week to discuss the restructuring.
The board meet next week to discuss the restructuring.
The board will meeting next week to discuss the restructuring.
The board are meet next week to discuss the restructuring.
questions.explanation: Present continuous expresses a fixed future arrangement: 'is meeting next week.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He said he will finish the project by Monday.
He said he would finish the project by Monday.
He said he would finished the project by Monday.
He said he would have finish the project by Monday.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts back to 'would': 'he said he would finish the project.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish my manager give more constructive feedback.
I wish my manager have given more constructive feedback.
I wish my manager gave more constructive feedback.
I wish my manager would give more constructive feedback as a habit.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past simple expresses regret about a present situation: 'I wish my manager gave more constructive feedback.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish I applied for that promotion last year.
I wish I have applied for that promotion last year.
I wish I would have applied for that promotion last year.
I wish I had applied for that promotion last year.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish I had applied for that promotion.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We had our office renovated last month.
We had renovated our office last month.
We had our office renovate last month.
We have our office renovated last month, right.
questions.explanation: Causative form: have + object + past participle shows someone else did the action: 'had our office renovated.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Never before the company had faced such fierce competition.
Never before had the company faced such fierce competition.
Never before did the company faced such fierce competition.
Never before has the company had faced such fierce competition.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials at the start trigger inversion: 'Never before had the company faced...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: HR is looking the complaint into.
HR is looking in to the complaint.
HR is looking into the complaint.
HR is looking into to the complaint.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means 'investigate' and is inseparable: 'looking into the complaint.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: What the team urgently need are clearer communication channels.
That the team urgently needs is clearer communication channels.
What the team urgently needs is clearer communication channels it.
What the team urgently needs is clearer communication channels.
questions.explanation: 'What' clefts take a singular verb when the complement is singular: 'What the team needs is clearer communication.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some employees prefer remote work, whereas others favor the office.
Some employees prefer remote work, whereas others favors the office.
Some employees prefer remote work whereas, others favor the office.
Some employees prefer remote work despite others favor the office.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two clauses and is followed directly by the subject: 'whereas others favor the office.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In spite the tight deadline, the team delivered excellent work.
In spite of the tight deadline, the team delivered excellent work.
Despite of the tight deadline, the team delivered excellent work.
In spite of the tight deadline, the team delivered excellent work though.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase: 'In spite of the tight deadline, the team delivered excellent work.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A number of surveys has linked flexible schedules to higher productivity.
The number of surveys have linked flexible schedules to higher productivity.
A number of surveys have linked flexible schedules to higher productivity.
A great number of surveys has linked flexible schedules to higher productivity.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb: 'a number of surveys have linked...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She spoke in behalf of the entire marketing team.
She spoke on behalf for the entire marketing team.
She spoke behalf of the entire marketing team.
She spoke on behalf of the entire marketing team.
questions.explanation: 'On behalf of' means 'representing someone': 'she spoke on behalf of the team.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The implementation of flexible hours improved staff morale significantly.
The implement of flexible hours improved staff morale significantly.
The implementing of flexible hours improved staff morale significantly.
The implementation of flexible hours improve staff morale significantly.
questions.explanation: Formal writing often nominalizes verbs into nouns: 'implement' becomes 'the implementation of...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting information about a job vacancy?
options: I'm writing to ask you about the job vacancy, ok?
I am writing to enquire about the job vacancy advertised on your website.
Just wanted to know about the job vacancy.
Hey, tell me about the job vacancy.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to enquire about...' is a standard formal opening for information requests.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about unpaid overtime?
options: I'm writing because I'm really mad about my unpaid overtime.
I want to complain about my unpaid overtime, it's bad.
I am writing to express my concern about unpaid overtime hours.
I am writing to express my concern about unpaid overtime hours, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use measured language such as 'I am writing to express my concern about...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The findings of the workplace survey were extreme alarming.
The findings of the workplace survey were extremely alarm.
The findings of the workplace survey were very much alarming.
The findings of the workplace survey were extremely alarming.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' (adverb) modifies the adjective 'alarming': 'were extremely alarming.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The new schedule is more flexible. Moreover, it boosts productivity.
The new schedule is more flexible, moreover it boosts productivity.
The new schedule is more flexible. Moreover it boosts productivity.
The new schedule is more flexible moreover, it boosts productivity.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'The new schedule is more flexible. Moreover, it boosts productivity.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You'd support a four-day work week, didn't you?
You'd support a four-day work week, wouldn't you?
You'd support a four-day work week, would you?
You'd support a four-day work week, wouldn't it?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'would' takes a negative tag: 'You'd support..., wouldn't you?'
